**Setting.** Operating units of multi-unit firms.

**Research question.** What determines unit performance in these firms, and in particular how does the decentralization of operating decisions affect unit performance, through which mechanisms, and under what conditions?

**Data.** `data.csv` with N = 1200 observations at the unit-year level. See the codebook for variables.

**Prior literature available to the team** (summaries of earlier studies in comparable settings; cite them by ID):

- **[L1]** Panel of 418 business units in 37 multi-unit firms. Higher share of operating decisions delegated from headquarters to the unit was associated with higher unit operating performance relative to plan (standardized b = +0.23, p < .01). - **[L2]** Survey of 265 units matched to market volatility data. The association between share of operating decisions delegated from headquarters to the unit and unit operating performance relative to plan was more positive when volatility of demand and competitive conditions in the unit's market was high (interaction b = +0.27, p < .05). Decentralized units are argued to adapt faster when conditions change.
- **[L3]** Cross-sectional study of 720 units. Higher hours the unit spends on formal strategic planning was associated with higher unit operating performance relative to plan (standardized b = +0.23, p < .01). The authors recommend formal planning routines.
- **[L4]** Decision-audit study of 1,900 decisions in 84 units. - **[L5]** Archival study of 3,400 unit-years. Higher average years of managerial experience in the unit leadership team was associated with higher unit operating performance relative to plan (standardized b = +0.24, p < .01).
